findings.title: Slots inside a date override bypass all busy-time checks
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot falls on a day that has a date override and the slot is inside the override window, `dateOverrideExist` is set to true and the function returns true immediately (lines 133-135), never reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at the bottom. Consequence: a fixed host (or any host) who has a calendar event or an accepted Cal booking during the override window will still be reported as available for that slot, allowing double bookings — the exact class of bug this PR claims to fix for round-robin. The override check should mark the slot as within-override and then still evaluate busy times.

findings.title: Working-hours check compares UTC slot hours to organizer-local working hours and computes wrong end
findings.body: The new working-hours validation computes `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute(); const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` — start and end are identical, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends past workingHour.endTime is never rejected (end should be start + eventLength). Additionally, `slotStartTime` is a UTC dayjs (time.utc()), so `hour()` returns the UTC hour, while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are minutes-since-midnight in the organizer's timezone. For any organizer not on UTC the comparison is off by the organizer's UTC offset, so valid slots get rejected and invalid ones accepted.

findings.title: Object-identity comparison of dayjs instances is always false
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct dayjs object references with `===`, which is always false regardless of values. The intended zero-length-override (unavailability) check is dead code and never fires; presumably `.isSame(...)` was meant.

findings.title: Selected-slots filter drops dateOverrides and workingHours, weakening availability check
findings.body: In the final selectedSlots filter (line ~581), checkIfIsAvailable is called with `busy`, `...availabilityCheckProps`, and `organizerTimeZone`, but without the host's `dateOverrides` or `workingHours`. For events with seat selection or reserved slots, the date-override logic just added elsewhere is not applied here, so behavior differs between the fixed/loose host checks and this path; slots that should be blocked by a fixed host's date override can still be returned in this branch.

findings.title: Override times that cross midnight after offset conversion produce inverted minute ranges
findings.body: The override startTime/endTime are computed as `hour() * 60 + minute()` after applying the invitee-organizer offset. If the shift moves the override start or end across midnight (e.g., an organizer override ending at 00:30 local), the minute-of-day arithmetic produces a wrong or inverted range (endTime < startTime), which buildSlots then discards (`if (start >= end) continue`) or clips incorrectly, silently dropping availability that should exist. There is no handling for day rollover introduced by the offset.

findings.title: No test for the round-robin fixed-host date-override fix described in the PR
findings.body: The PR's headline fix (date overrides of fixed hosts constraining round-robin availability) has no corresponding test: the only new test re-checks the personal-event timezone behavior, and the existing ROUND_ROBIN tests use plain IstWorkHours schedules without date overrides for the fixed host. A regression in the checkIfIsAvailable changes (e.g., the busy-time bypass or the broken working-hours comparison) would not be caught for the round-robin scenario the PR claims to fix.
